about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about multiplying and factoring polynomials. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-21), waiting for owner review.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the middle term when multiplying: (x + 4)² = x² + 16, (x + 3)(x + 5) = x² + 15.
Adds the last terms instead of multiplying them: (x + 3)(x + 5) = x² + 8x + 8.
Loses the sign of the last term: (x + 3)(x − 5) = x² − 2x + 15.
Multiplies only the outer (or only the inner) terms for the middle: (2x + 1)(x + 3) = 2x² + 6x + 3.
Divides only one term by the common factor: 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 9).
Subtracts the common factor instead of dividing: 6x + 9 = 3(3x + 6).
Gets the signs in the factors backwards: x² + 7x + 12 as (x − 3)(x − 4).
Finds numbers that multiply to c but don't add to b: x² + 7x + 12 as (x + 2)(x + 6).
Factors x² − 25 as (x − 5)(x − 5) or (x + 5)(x + 5): one factor needs + and the other −.
Puts the right numbers in the wrong factors for ax² + bx + c, so the middle term comes out wrong: 2x² + 7x + 3 as (2x + 3)(x + 1).
